quote.text: The quality will be remembered long after the price is forgotten.
quote.author: Sir Henry Royce, co-founder of Rolls-Royce; a standing maxim of the marque

stories.headline: Iran and Oman Draw a Line Through Hormuz. The Oil Price Fell Again.
stories.dek: After six months of the war choking the world's most important oil chokepoint, the two coastal states agreed a temporary corridor, a revenue split and a joint mine-clearing effort. There is one hole in it: the strait stays shut until Washington honours a deal it has not yet signed. Crude fell a third straight session anyway.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · Priced, and Waiting
stories.headline: A Record Chip Quarter the Market Had Already Bought, and One Man's First Jackson Hole
stories.dek: The day hangs between two poles — Nvidia last night, Warsh tomorrow. Gold sits near a three-month high with the dollar firm, both hedges bid at once. The swing variable isn't growth or liquidity. It's the price of money, and it's set on Friday.

stories.headline: The Hobby Where a Thirty-Four-Dollar Pen Can Shame a Five-Hundred-Dollar One
stories.dek: It starts with a single wet nib gliding across good paper at almost no pressure, or an ink that flashes red-gold in the light. Then you learn the pen was the cheap part. Welcome to a bottomless, self-aware, gloriously analogue descent — pens, then nibs, then inks, then paper.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Boom and Its Bill
stories.headline: The Export Machine Is Running Hot. The Central Bank Just Named the Price.
stories.dek: July shipments jumped a quarter on the year on the same AI wave lifting Wall Street — and the growth forecast was torn up upward. Then MAS said the quiet part: core inflation rises from here, into early 2027. A cheaper barrel from the Gulf is the only relief in sight.

stories.headline: A Bag Is a Hide, a Stitch and a Story. Learn to Read the First Two.
stories.dek: "Full-grain," "Italian," "heritage" — the words that sell a leather bag are the ones that hide who made it. Judge the tannage and the seam, and a four-hundred-dollar workshop briefcase outlives a three-thousand-dollar monogram. Here is the category from the hide up.

stories.kicker: Technology · The Print Everyone Waited For
stories.headline: Nvidia Beat Every Line. "Compute Is Revenue," Said the Boss. The Stock Fell.
stories.dek: Ninety-six billion dollars in a quarter, a hundred-and-eight-billion guide that assumes nothing from China, and a gross margin of seventy-five per cent — and the shares slipped after hours. When the biggest number in the market is already in the price, a record is just confirmation.

stories.kicker: The Kit · A Satellite on Every Wrist
stories.headline: Garmin's Flagship Goes All-Titanium and Puts an Emergency Beacon on Every Model
stories.dek: The fēnix 9 landed on Monday from a thousand dollars, with built-in satellite messaging pushed down the whole line for the first time. The real story is not the case metal — it is that the beacon no longer costs extra.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · Objects Worth the Wait
stories.headline: Eight DACs, Twenty-Eight Hours, and a Price Astell&Kern Won't Say Yet
stories.dek: The PD5 doubles the digital-to-analogue converters of the five-star player it replaces and adds a feature that listens to the room. Everything about it is known except the one number that decides whether it is a bargain or a folly.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · The Sleeper and the Smash
stories.headline: A First-Timer's Road-to-Nowhere Horror Becomes the Year's Best-Reviewed Fright
stories.dek: "It Ends" opened wide on Friday to a critics' score no horror film has touched in 2026. On the same weekend a global girl group is set to top the album chart with the reviews running the other way — the week's neat inversion of who gets to say a thing is good.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Lever That Actually Moves
stories.headline: The New Study Says It Is Sleep, Not Screens, That Moves a Twelve-Year-Old's Mind Most
stories.dek: Among four daily habits — sleep, screen time, activity, diet — one did far more of the work linking a child's mental health to how they do at school and with friends. The panic has been aimed at the wrong target. General guidance for a Secondary One parent, not medical advice.

stories.kicker: Fitness · Five Minutes at a Time
stories.headline: The Study Everyone Re-Posted Is Old. The Better Idea for the Time-Poor Is Snacks.
stories.dek: The strength "sweet spot" that flooded feeds this month is a June paper on its second lap. The genuinely useful move for a busy mid-forties optimiser is smaller and better-evidenced: bouts of hard effort under five minutes, twice a day. Not medical advice.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking — Home and Away
The Certainty Economy
stories.dek: A generation of Thais, priced out of the old ladders, is buying luck by the amulet — shopped online, curated on TikTok, and sold back to them by banks, telcos and the state. It is the country's fastest-growing consumer category, and it is booming precisely because the real economy has stopped delivering.
